item.title: Fast is the easy part. Here is why you can trust KPipe with your offsets.
item.description:
KPipe, part 3 of 3: a simpler way to structure consumers · the first benchmarks · fast is the easy part

Last time I benchmarked KPipe I ended with a warning about my own numbers. Single runs moved 5 to 40 percent between iterations. There was no latency-percentile data. I told you to read the percentages as one-sigma indicators and not to quote the absolute throughput at anyone.

That was the honest thing to say at the time, and it was also a promissory note. This post is me paying it. The numbers here come from a quiesced machine - no browser, no IDE indexing, on mains power - with five JMH forks instead of one, the full workMicros sweep out to 100 ms per record, and latency percentiles alongside. The raw JSON and a dated markdown snapshot are committed in benchmarks/results/ as always. Where the last post had ±5-40% error bars, this one has ±0.1-6% on nearly every cell.
